proposed_from.topic: Projective copula-excitation frontier for scale-erased causal discovery. Fix p and an invariant acyclic linear-Gaussian SCM with unknown baseline innovation variances. Across environments, innovation coordinates receive known positive multipliers, but each site releases only its Gaussian copula/correlation matrix, with unrelated marginal scales. Define the projective Cholesky fiber of compatible directed supports. Prove the sharp universal generic criterion: every pair of multiplier-profile columns is projectively distinct iff every DAG is generically a singleton of this fiber; give explicit nonisomorphic fork/chain twins when profiles tie. Construct canonical order predictors and exact fiber recovery, including an O(Ep^3) conditional-pair algorithm on generic complete DAGs, then invert Kendall-tau rank summaries into honest graph confidence sets under explicit separation. Consumer: FedCDH-style federated summary sharing and the backShift workflow, which can accept rank-only site releases exactly above the excitation boundary. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Reference-environment Cholesky normalization was derived to eliminate continuous scale search: each candidate order determines one canonical standardized recursive model and predicts every other correlation matrix. Reversed-edge polynomial witnesses give an all-p generic uniqueness spine under pairwise nonproportional schedule columns; tied columns yield an explicit positive fork/chain counterfamily. Exact computations recovered all 25 labeled three-node DAGs across 300 rational parameter choices, checked diagonal-gauge equivariance and weak/singular regimes, and verified conditional-pair peeling through p=6. No direct primary-source or internal collision was found. Compressed standard claims, the all-p polynomial argument, sparse-graph computation, and the uniform inference perturbation layer still require independent audit. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform Cholesky-predictor perturbation bounds and close the finite-sample graph-confidence theorem with an explicit fallback convention and normalized beta-min margin. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct the canonical-order reduction under arbitrary positive reference rescaling and reproduce the p=3 covariance example with d_1=(1,4,9) and all five wrong-order exclusions; any legal model outside the canonical list or matching wrong order stops this spine. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest multiple-environment comparator is Montagna2025InvariancePrinciple, Section 3, Theorem 1, which identifies the graph from full environment densities through score and Hessian information and requires two auxiliary environments. The present work observes only independently standardized correlation orbits and proves the reference-plus-one-environment frontier. BACKSHIFT Theorem 1 is another close template, but its covariance differences are not determined by independently gauged correlations. The new object is a canonical projective Cholesky fiber: each order yields a unique reference-standardized matrix \(B^{\pi}(R_0)\) and predicts every other correlation from only \(d\). Pairwise projective separation makes every nontopological match a nonzero polynomial, while tied profiles yield exact reverse-edge and positive fork--chain twins, producing a universal generic if-and-only-if frontier. GnIES arXiv:2211.14897v4, Theorem 6, is only an informed-by full-distribution comparator, the distinct TaebEtAl2024Latent paper is not conflated with it, and PetersEtAl2016InvariantPrediction targets invariant conditional response laws rather than this whole-DAG correlation quotient. Park2020ConditionalVariance and YinEtAl2024HNM require scale-bearing conditional variances and do not subsume calibrated correlation prediction. The positivity, signed squared-cross-product, and order-compatibility checks belong only to the exhaustive algorithm construction and are not claimed as a theorem contribution. The conditional-pair theorem contributes the independent local completeness proof and stagewise \(O(Ep^3)\) operation count. The inference layer treats bounded normalized excitation as a novel design regularity, consistently thresholds \(B^0=H_0BH_0^{-1}\), uses the same unit-free margin in its class, fallback, and singleton condition, and relies on LiuEtAl2012NPNskeptic Theorem 4.2 only for the Kendall correlation event.

seed_details.one_line: Characterize pairwise projective separation as necessary and sufficient for every labeled DAG to be generically a singleton of the correlation-only projective Cholesky fiber.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Does pairwise projective distinctness exactly characterize universal generic recovery after independent site scaling?
seed_details.anchor_read: BACKSHIFT Sections 1--3, Theorem 1, Appendix A, and the conclusion; GnIES Sections 1--3, Theorem 1, Appendix A.5, and Section 6; FedCDH Section 3.3, Theorem 8, and its conclusion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace covariance-difference joint diagonalization by reference-correlation modified Cholesky normalization, then separate every nontopological order with a reversed-edge polynomial witness.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining known variance intervention, Gaussian copula, correlation-only, diagonal scaling, Cholesky order, and causal DAG found covariance-scale or ordinary copula-MEC results but no exact target--method pair.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from BACKSHIFT Theorem 1 because the same pairwise noncollinearity minors appear.
seed_details.rebuttal: BACKSHIFT's input is a family of covariance differences on one common scale; those differences are not functionals of independently gauged correlations. The orderwise canonical reduction and fork--chain necessity family are new proof steps specific to acyclicity and scale erasure.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The graph is the target, so M18 is primary; M6 is justified by both a generic sufficiency proof and a positive-dimensional necessity family.

seed_details.one_line: Propagate simultaneous Kendall errors through every order predictor and invert the resulting bands into an honest graph confidence set with explicit fallback.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Can rank-correlation errors be controlled uniformly through projective Cholesky prediction near weak excitation and poor conditioning?
seed_details.anchor_read: Nonparanormal SKEPTIC Sections 2--4; Mitra--Zhang Theorems 1--2; Wang--Kolar--Drton Sections 1, 4--5, Theorem 1, and Section 7.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compose inverse, Schur-complement, triangular-resolvent, and correlation-normalization perturbation inequalities uniformly over all orders before applying one simultaneous Kendall event.
seed_details.destination_search: Rank-correlation papers control matrix inputs, and ordering-confidence papers invert residual tests, but no located result controls the nonlinear known-schedule predictor family or supplies its all-DAG fallback.
seed_details.referee_objection: Routine delta-method propagation of the Kendall bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: The map ranges over all principal submatrices and orders and includes inverses and diagonal normalizations; uniform constants diverge at named eigenvalue and excitation boundaries, so pointwise differentiability does not prove simultaneous finite-sample coverage.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: M8 is attached to the M18 structural functional and the deterministic modulus is stated as a separate theorem-level object.

seed_details.one_line: Quotient a removed-set recursion by projective Cholesky fragments to enumerate every sparse compatible support exactly once.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Prove a local continuation congruence for equality of projective Cholesky fragments, replacing deduplication only after complete orders are formed.
seed_details.destination_search: Graphical MEC enumeration has canonical parents, but the destination equivalence depends on numerical standardized regression fragments and can merge distinct order prefixes only after zero coefficients appear.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from standard reverse search on permutations.
seed_details.rebuttal: Permutation adjacency does not prevent many orders from returning one support; the missing content is a generatable quotient parent and a proof that local fragment equality preserves exactly the same continuation outputs.

seed_details.one_line: Characterize the maximal jointly identifiable quotient of the DAG and an unknown positive multiplier-profile matrix from environment-indexed copulas.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace equality of covariance models by equality of positive diagonal-scaling orbits and separate recovery of projective schedule directions from their matching to vertices.

seed_details.anchor_read: The prior proposal's positive-semidefinite boundary caveat was read together with BACKSHIFT Appendix A's open-neighborhood necessity perturbation and conclusion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace positive Schur-complement Cholesky normalization by simultaneous-congruence strata and calculate the residual symmetry group when pivots vanish.
seed_details.destination_search: Singular simultaneous-congruence theory describes feasibility, but no located causal result classifies exact support fibers for each zero-innovation pattern under correlation-only release.
seed_details.referee_objection: The positive-definite theorem extends by continuity.
seed_details.rebuttal: At a zero pivot the canonical regression map is undefined and graph distinctions can disappear discontinuously, so closure of the interior singleton statement does not give boundary identification.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The intended region is a named rank stratum, not a single singular witness.
seed_details.status: dropped because it requires a different normalization theory

seed_details.one_line: Classify the real algebraic exceptional fibers that remain when all multiplier profiles are projectively distinct.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: What exact graph equivalences occur on nongeneric cancellation loci?
seed_details.anchor_read: GnIES Section 3's graphical equivalence characterization and Peters--Bühlmann's recursive identifiability proof were read to locate the first step that loses information on cancellation strata.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the nonzero-polynomial exclusion argument by a local covered-edge analysis of the common zero set of all order-prediction minors.
seed_details.destination_search: Partial-homoscedastic and interventional MEC papers classify graph equivalence from full covariance laws, not the real zero-set components of independently standardized multi-environment predictors.
seed_details.referee_objection: The exceptional locus is just unfaithfulness.
seed_details.rebuttal: Predictor cancellations can involve cross-environment excitation ratios even when each environment is faithful, so the locus is not identical to ordinary conditional-independence unfaithfulness.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This would require a generic-region theorem plus a substantive classification, not one hand-tuned cancellation.
seed_details.status: dropped because a full real-locus classification is not needed for the sharp universal generic theorem

seed_details.one_line: Extend two-environment conditional-pair peeling from complete DAGs to sparse graphs satisfying an observable local uniqueness certificate.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: When does the local pair-odds rule avoid factorial sparse-order search?
seed_details.anchor_read: Peters--Bühlmann's recursive source proof and BACKSHIFT's cubic assignment step were read as algorithmic templates, including their conclusions on computational scope.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Derive a sparse local certificate ensuring that each Schur-complement state has one admissible root or one equivalence class of commuting roots.
seed_details.destination_search: Precision-based and equal-variance peeling use different local gaps; no located method uses known profile ratios in conditional correlation odds after sitewise scale erasure.
seed_details.referee_objection: A generic sparse DAG has a unique source, so ordinary peeling applies.
seed_details.rebuttal: Sparse DAGs generically may have several roots and missing edges create zero pair odds, so uniqueness must be certified modulo commuting removals rather than assumed.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed names the local structural certificate sought and does not claim a routine complete-to-sparse extension.
seed_details.status: dropped and narrowed to the exact-once open question

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected kernel sits between covariance-shift identification, recursive Gaussian-DAG identification, and rank-based graph inference. BACKSHIFT Section 2.4 and Theorem 1 turn full covariance differences into a uniquely normalized joint diagonalizer under pairwise noncollinear intervention profiles; its Appendix A proof inspired the necessity--sufficiency architecture, but arbitrary site gauges destroy its input. Peters and Bühlmann's Theorem 1 supplies the orderwise conditional-variance and triangular-factorization precedent. GnIES Sections 1--3 and Theorem 1 define the competing-model equivalence perspective under full Gaussian environment distributions and unknown targets; the scale-erased known-schedule fiber is not one of its equivalence classes. FedCDH Section 3.3 and Theorem 8 establish a federated summary consumer, but use covariance tensors rather than rank-only correlations. Liu et al. Sections 2--4 provide the Kendall sine link and uniform entrywise rate. Mitra and Zhang Theorems 1--2 provide spectral and simultaneous-submatrix rank-correlation deviations. Wang, Kolar, and Drton Sections 4--5 and Theorem 1 supply the confidence-set inversion template, but their validity is asymptotic and based on residual independence. Afsari's joint-diagonalization perturbation theory explains why profile conditioning matters but does not control modified Cholesky predictions. Hauser and Bühlmann's coloring and separation construction informs a distinct schedule-design extension. The bounded target--method search found no closer paper whose theorem recovers an acyclic linear-Gaussian exact support from known multiplicative excitations after every environment is independently standardized.
